title: Marlin Aero pilot integration journal
content:
Quick log from kickoff + early troubleshooting for Marlin Aero pilot (onboarding contact: Alex Rivera, Sr. Systems Eng). Purpose: on-prem inference proxy for maintenance-assistant (diagnostics summarization) with strict airgap and 95th percentile < 300ms per short query target for pilot. Notes are messy — for my reference and handoff to Marco/Ethan.

1) Meeting recap (2026-01-27 initial call):
- Stakeholders: Alex (infra), Priya (product, not our Priya), Ray (compliance).
- Pilot scope: small fleet support tool -> short prompts, 40–60 tokens typical, some longer context for fault logs (up to ~1.2k tokens occasionally).
- Security: airgapped environment, must support customer KMS (HSM) and no telemetry leaving network.
- Ops: want canary + rollback, prefer dedicated GPU pool on-site, but limited ops headcount so we provide a private control plane that can be run in their VPC and a minimal on-prem proxy that stores no logs.

2) First pass requirements (explicit):
- API compatibility: Redwood hosted API surface (text/generate + streaming) — they want same SDK surface to minimize rewrite.
- Latency SLO: 95th < 300ms for <1000-token requests, 99th < 700ms with fallback.
- Throughput: pilot ~ 40 rps peak, expected growth to 120 rps in 3mo.
- Model: start with open-llama-7B-quant (we recommended a Redwood-verified variant).
- Cost/ops: prefer quantized CPU fallback for very low priority background tasks.

3) Environment notes (collected from Alex):
- Hardware: 2x A40 on-prem (single node), older switch (1Gb management, 10Gb data), limited NFS quota.
- OS: RHEL 8.6 hardened image; no root on inference node (ops will run container runtime).
- Networking: restricted egress, only allowed outbound to our control plane IPs on port 443 (mutual TLS).

4) Early gotchas / risks we surfaced: (brain dump)
- KV cache warmup: with only 2 GPUs and continuous short queries, we need to tune prefix caching aggressively; otherwise cold-cache tail latency spikes will blow SLO. Action: propose aggressive local KV caching + prewarm script for known prompt prefixes.
- Model memory: 7B quant still hitting 30GB inference working set with current kernel (unexpected on A40) — may need 4-bit or alternative kernel compile. Follow-up with serving-runtime team ticket (JIRA-1299) to test kernel selection.
- Filesystem constraints: their NFS is flaky under many small writes; our shard persistence must fallback to in-memory checkpointing with delayed flush.
- Telemetry: they insist on no PII telemetry. Must provide audit-only telemetry (counts, latencies) and local-only debug logs. Add a telemetry opt-in toggle in config.

5) Performance notes from quick local run (Ethan ran a bench on similar box 2026-02-05):
- Model: rwi/open-7b-rwq (approx config)
- Batch size 1 steady-state: p50 ~ 68ms, p95 ~ 420ms (cold-cache p95 ~ 1.2s)
- SSE throughput with 2 GPUs (sharded): sustained 35–45 rps for short prompts; per-token cost still high due to kernel inefficiency in attention.
- Hypothesis: custom kernel + KV prefetch should drop p95 cold to ~250–300ms. Need bench PR from serving-runtime.

6) Prompt / functional must-haves (product):
- Deterministic rerank endpoint: they want to run diagnostics -> 3 candidate completions -> rerank by safety & brevity. We need to expose a reranker + explainability fields (score + reason).
- Structured output: JSON schema enforcement (we support that via structured output guardrails). Provide examples for their log->summary mapping.

7) Draft onboarding checklist (for pilot):
- [ ] Confirm signed NDA + airgap checklist (legal)
- [ ] Confirm control plane firewall rules and IP allowlist (Alex)
- [ ] Provision image with our on-prem runtime + agent (Marco)
- [ ] Run tuning bench (Ethan) with their sample logs (Priya to provide sample corpus)
- [ ] Enable KV prewarm script; simulate production prefix distribution
- [ ] Document telemetry configuration & create opt-in config
- [ ] Add canary rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks (latency + errors)

8) Short-term action assignments (owners):
- Marco: build RHEL container image, include our restricted-file-mode & HSM integration (due 2026-02-07)
- Ethan: reproduce perf numbers on their sample corpus, attach bench traces to JIRA-1299 (due 2026-02-10)
- Me (Sofia): draft customer-facing pilot runbook + security addendum; collect sample prompts/schema from Priya (due 2026-02-03)
- Solutions Eng lead (Priya N.): coordinate legal onboarding + runbook review (ongoing)

9) Notes-to-self / ideas: (unpolished)
- Consider shipping a tiny local redis instance for KV persistence rather than relying on their NFS — simpler and more robust for pilot.
- Could expose a "low-priority" queue that routes background long-context requests to CPU-only quantized fallback to save GPU cycles.
- Fallback policy: when p95 > 700ms or GPU queueing > 80%, route to smaller model (e.g., 3B) and attach a flag response.warned_model_swap=true so product can surface to user.

10) Unresolved questions (to clarify with Alex / Ray):
- HSM integration details: do they want our control plane to hold keys or only a local HSM? (security asks local only)
- Acceptable telemetry granularity: are aggregated counts + anonymized latency enough or do they need richer audit trails?
- What are their exact RPO/RTO expectations around the pilot node (they said "24h" but need specificity).

11) Meeting follow-ups (scheduled):
- 2026-02-02: deep-dive with infra (Marco + Ethan + Alex) to run bench and discuss kernel options.
- 2026-02-09: compliance sync (Ray + legal + Priya N.) for telemetry & HSM contract language.

12) Quick sample prompt + expected structured output (for Priya to hand to us):
- Prompt: "Explain the root cause of fault 0xA32 in lay terms, include affected subsystems and remediation steps (max 4 bullets)."
- Expected JSON schema: {"summary": string, "affected_subsystems": [string], "remediation": [string], "confidence": number}
- Note: implement schema validator in proxy layer to reject non-conforming outputs and fall back to another prompt + model if invalid.

End-of-journal snapshot. Will prune and turn into a tidy runbook once kernel bench results come back. For now: keep everything local, no sampling telemetry turned on, and push the prewarm and fallback policy as the highest-risk mitigation.
